title: Complete integral objects in canonical constant coefficient coordinates
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite-dimensional field extension E/Q_l, and let X be any scheme. Use the completed integral coefficient sheaf and its actual positive quotient tower [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the bounded constructible derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and the canonical restriction functor H and constant coefficient datum [def-sf-constant-completed-reduction-transport], on the published small-site model with its local ideal-completeness predicate [def-zl-compact-support-small-site-morphism], [def-pur-adic-site-strict-quotient-interface]. For every object K of that integral category, H(K) is locally derived complete for the lifted uniformizer ideal on the small site. For any two objects K,L of that category, the actual map Hom(K,L) to Hom(H(K),H(L)) induced by H is bijective. There are no finite-field, Tor-amplitude, morphism, compactification, or word hypotheses.

lean.statement:
theorem integralConstantCompleteTransport
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (∀ K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X,
      (sfCbcSite X).IsComplete _ (sfCbcModelIdeal (constantDatum l E))
        ((H l E X).obj K.obj)) ∧
    (∀ K L : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X,
      Function.Bijective (fun m : K.obj ⟶ L.obj ↦ (H l E X).map m))
